data.narrative:
Ranovus is a Series D+ stage semiconductor company that has raised $236M to date, including a $36M strategic investment fund grant in August 2025. The target operates within a Chips & Semiconductors sector that includes 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers, though narrowly filtered peer sets prove sparse for direct valuation anchoring.

Two standard triangulation methods were assessed but could not be applied. Peer-median analysis is inapplicable: while 12 same-sector peers exist in the Chips & Semiconductors universe, none of the narrow filters—same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier—yielded three or more datapoints required for a robust median. Public-comp anchoring is similarly constrained: the three public semiconductor comparables traded at a median P/S of 21.4x, but Ranovus does not disclose revenue, precluding application of this multiple to establish a valuation range.

The absence of applicable quantitative methods reflects a structural constraint common to early-stage deep-tech: Ranovus lacks both sufficiently dense private peer data at its stage and public disclosure needed for multiple-based anchoring. Any valuation at this stage would require supplementary methods—such as DCF modeling with disclosed unit economics, or qualitative expert assessment of technical defensibility—neither of which are supported by the provided dataset. The analysis cannot responsibly produce a valuation range without additional financial or comparable-company data.
